key_insight: A moving fluid can make a quantum vortex ring acquire unusual energy-momentum states, including negative effective mass, which may trigger coupled vortex behavior relevant to turbulence onset.
engineering_relevance: The model offers a physics-based way to estimate a critical Reynolds-like threshold for quantum turbulence in pipe flows and vortex-ring systems.
method: Analyze the vortex-ring energy spectrum E(p) as a function of background flow velocity v.
Use a new quantization scheme for classical closed vortex filaments to derive effective masses from the spectrum.
Compare a quantum Reynolds-number analogue against its critical single-vortex value to predict allowed states.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical spectrum analysis showing states with negative and very large effective masses, plus paired vortex states with finite total effective mass.
watch_item: The results are model-based and depend on the proposed quantization framework, so experimental validation is still needed before using the threshold criterion in practice.
paper_title: Quantum vortex in a fluid flow: negative effective mass and a novel mechanism for turbulence formation
